aspect: A stereotype about honesty is worse than one about competence
description: Incompetence can be disproved by performance. Dishonesty cannot be disproved at all - every success can be re-read as a better deception, which is why the usual advice to work harder does not resolve it.
energy_note: You cannot out-perform an accusation of lying.

description: Volunteering references, receipts, certificates and screenshots before anyone asks. It is exhausting, it is rational, and it reads to the recipient as slightly odd - which is its own cost.
energy_note: Proving yourself before anyone has doubted you, and looking strange doing it.

description: Simultaneously assumed to be a potential fraud and a potential victim - suspected for the nationality and patronised for the gender, frequently by the same person in the same conversation.
energy_note: Suspected and pitied, at once, by the same colleague.

aspect: Anger at the actual fraudsters, with nowhere to go
description: Resentment among ordinary Nigerians toward the people who built the reputation is intense, and voicing it abroad reads as confirming the stereotype rather than distancing from it.
energy_note: Furious at them, and unable to say so without sounding like them.

aspect: Children inherit it without the context
description: A second-generation child is asked about the prince joke in a playground in a country their parents chose, with no framework for it and no memory of Nigeria at all.

aspect: It suppresses the visibility that would eventually change it
description: Starting the company, taking the platform, publishing under your own name - the things that would replace the stereotype are exactly the things it makes expensive.
energy_note: The cure is the thing it prices out.

description: He stops putting Lagos in his signature and starts writing 'GMT+1'. Response rates improve. He knows exactly what that means and has never mentioned the change to anyone.
energy_note: Removing the city from the signature, and it working.
